what: DECISIONS #3 router gate: does nanomem's IVF cell router ship ON by default?

protocol.gate: DECISIONS #3: engage the router by default above n_exhaustive only if the 95% CI lower bound of (router - exhaustive) recall@4 is >= -1.0 pt at the chosen default budget, on the 71,433-doc corpus in random insertion order after compact(recluster=True).
protocol.gate_is_necessary_not_sufficient: A router exists to be cheaper than the scan it replaces. Passing the recall gate earns the router the right to be considered; phases B-D decide whether turning it on is an improvement or a regression.
protocol.metric: recall@4 over the 2 gold paragraphs per question
protocol.isolation: one subprocess per arm; ru_maxrss delta measured inside it

prep.recluster: nanomem.routing.recluster(V, cell_target=50) -- identical to VaultEngine.compact(recluster=True) at block_capacity=50

phase_D_synthetic_214299.distractor_recipe: DECISIONS #16: v + N(0, 0.35^2), re-normalised, np.random.default_rng(0); SYNTHETIC

phase_A_random_layout_control.per_question_encoding: one digit per question, 0/1/2 of the 2 gold paragraphs in the top 4; recall@4 = mean/2, paired difference = (router - exhaustive) * 50 pt

gate_definition.recall: 95% CI lower bound of (router - exhaustive) recall@4 >= -1.0 pt
gate_definition.reproducible: routed p50 < exhaustive p50 in EVERY replicate

decision.recall_gate_evidence: 13 of 30 swept configs clear CI lower bound >= -1.0 pt; cheapest is cell_target=12 beam_frac=0.10 at 77.00% recall@4 vs 77.30% exhaustive, delta -0.30 pt CI [-0.55, -0.1]
decision.reproducible_gate_evidence: off: p50 median 2.0305 ms (1.9656-3.5470), speed-up vs off median 1.000x (1.000x-1.000x), faster in 0 of 5 replicates; auto_shipped_budget: p50 median 3.6151 ms (3.5187-5.9449), speed-up vs off median 0.562x (0.559x-0.597x), faster in 0 of 5 replicates; auto_gate_budget: p50 median 2.1256 ms (2.1019-3.5305), speed-up vs off median 0.958x (0.935x-1.005x), faster in 1 of 5 replicates
decision.amortised_gate_evidence: auto_shipped_budget never breaks even: it is 1.5846 ms SLOWER per query than the scan it replaces; auto_gate_budget never breaks even: it is 0.0951 ms SLOWER per query than the scan it replaces
decision.one_sentence: DECISIONS #3's RECALL gate PASSES -- 13 of 30 swept budgets are within 1.0 pt of the exact scan and the cheapest is 77.00% against 77.30% -- but the router still ships OFF, because it fails the reproducible and amortised tests.

latency_confirmation_quiet_machine.why: phases B-D re-measured on a quiet machine; the original run was taken at 1-min load average 19.6-25.7 on 12 cores, which is not a fair floor for a latency verdict. Phase A (recall) is deterministic and is NOT re-run.

phase_D_synthetic_214299.distractor_recipe: DECISIONS #16: v + N(0, 0.35^2), re-normalised, np.random.default_rng(0); SYNTHETIC

engine_latency_replicates.why: the two single readings of phase C disagreed on the sign of the router's speed-up (0.923x loaded, 1.134x quiet), so the comparison is repeated as independent runs and the spread is reported

phase_A_rerun_check.what: the re-run against the numbers already in the file. Phase A is deterministic, so every delta here should be 0.0; a non-zero row is a finding, not a rounding.
phase_A_rerun_check.note: phase A exercises routing.GlobalCellRouter and numpy only -- no engine, no container -- so the engine version it ran under cannot change its arithmetic. It is recorded because the top-level engine_version belongs to the ORIGINAL full run, not to this re-run.
